about: Narration for the one-off Belle Gunness Halloween video (Oct. 20, 2026). Facts checked against Wikipedia's Belle Gunness article, Roadside America and the La Porte County Historical Society: the April 28, 1908 fire, her three children and a woman's body in the ashes, the remains of at least 11 more people on the farm, at least 14 victims, sightings for years and inconclusive DNA tests. Pushing a change to this file on the belle-video branch records it again (.github/workflows/belle-voice.yml).

lines.say: This is La Porte's scariest true story.
A widow named Belle Gunness bought a farm just outside La Porte.
She ran newspaper ads for a husband. Men came from across the Midwest to meet her. Many were never seen again.
On April 28, 1908, her farmhouse burned. In the ashes were her three children, and the body of a woman.
Then searchers dug up the farm. They found the remains of at least eleven more people.
But was that woman really Belle? People said they saw her alive for years. Even DNA tests couldn't settle it.
Her story is on display at the La Porte County Historical Society Museum. Happy Halloween.
